why: THE /sorted DOOR AND THE EMISSION GATE DISAGREE ABOUT WHAT A COMPLETE WATCHME SPEC IS, AND THE DOOR IS THE WEAKER ONE. skills/sorted/door.py:65 declares _WATCHME_FIELDS = (object, trigger, enough, carrier, consumer) — Akien's five — and refuses a spec missing any of them. cairn/base/watchme_spec.py:66 declares BERTH_FIELD = 'probe' and its own header says so explicitly: 'Not one of Akien's five — it is what makes ARMED measurable.' So a SIXTH field is mandatory at the crossing and unchecked at the cast. MEASURED TONIGHT, n=2 in one session: both tickets cast at /sorted on 2026-08-05 (a-claim-carries-its-provenance and a-concept-piece-has-a-voyage) fired CLEAN through the door with five-field specs, and minutes later cairn/base/proofs/test_watchme_spec.py went RED on both — 'WATCHME(<object>) spec names no probe — the emission gate resolves ARMED from a path, so a spec with no berth cannot be gated'. Two casts, two clean firings, two reds. The door's own module docstring states the principle it just failed to apply: 'a drifted string refused here costs one fix; the same string refused at its first crossing costs a dead voyage.' THE LIVED SYMPTOM: you do everything right — you fire the door, it passes, you file the ticket with its berth — and then the corpus proof reds on the ticket you just cast, for a field the door never asked for. The door printed a berth path, which reads as a seal. THE SHAPE WORTH CARRYING: this is a CHECK WEAKER THAN THE CLAIM IT CERTIFIES, which is the exact subject of the unconfirmed ruling decisions/2026-08-05-a-check-is-worth-its-mesh. The door does not merely miss the field; it certifies the packet complete.

occurrences.identity: skills/sorted/door.py::judge_packet — _WATCHME_FIELDS is one field short of the emission gate's demand
occurrences.how_found: bin/cmd/test full suite run 2026-08-05 evening, immediately after casting two tickets through the door. test_the_real_ticket_corpus_is_not_retro_redded named both new tickets by id. Not a hypothesis — the proof printed the two ids and the reason.

measured_evidence.door_accepts: both casts returned exit 0 with berths: sorted-20260805T204251-5755540bfe89 (a-claim-carries-its-provenance) and sorted-20260805T204721-f3b85a042be7 (a-concept-piece-has-a-voyage). The second fired clean on its FIRST attempt, so nothing in the refusal path was involved.
measured_evidence.gate_refuses: cairn/base/proofs/test_watchme_spec.py::test_the_real_ticket_corpus_is_not_retro_redded, RED with both ids; 13/14 green in that file. After adding `probe` to both tickets: 14/14 green.
measured_evidence.the_corpus_already_conforms: every OTHER cast ticket carrying a five-field spec already has `probe` — slate-compiles-from-the-world, skills-migrate-one-blow, engine-runs-one-block, logger-for-bash, the-deposit-rides-the-read, watchme-emits-a-probe, sorted-becomes-a-learning-block, intent-becomes-a-learning-block. So the convention is settled and only the door does not know it. That also explains why this was never caught: every prior cast was authored by someone who happened to include the field.
measured_evidence.why_the_door_missed_it: HYPOTHESIS, labelled (Law 3): the door was written to enforce AKIEN'S FIVE, and watchme_spec.py's sixth field arrived from a different ticket (watchme-emits-a-probe, 2026-07-30, piece c-ii) with its own header noting it is deliberately not one of the five. Two correct local decisions; nobody owned the seam between them.
measured_evidence.not_verified: whether the door's OTHER watchme checks match the gate — the object/summons agreement and the exemption-referent rule were not diffed against watchme_spec.py field by field. Only the field LIST was.

occurrences.already_done: Both tickets corrected on disk (probe paths named, with a probe_note recording that a path is a COMMITMENT and ARMED is measured at the crossing, not at the cast). The two BERTHS were deliberately NOT edited — they are records of the firing as it happened (Law 7); the ticket is the record of truth the gate reads. test_watchme_spec.py 14/14 green after.
occurrences.the_fix_not_taken_tonight: Adding 'probe' to _WATCHME_FIELDS is a one-line change and was NOT made. It would change what the door refuses, which is behaviour, and the door's own proof fixtures carry five-field specs that would start failing — that is a build with a proof, not an overnight edit. It also wants a decision the one-liner hides: the door should probably resolve its field list FROM watchme_spec.py rather than restate it (Law 1 — the settled answer lives once), which is the difference between fixing this instance and fixing the class.
